From a foot path
to explicit control.

What changed between my Python prototype and the inspected C++ controller: equations, frames, command interfaces, and checks.

Earlier Python: turn a foot path into position targets

The inspected Python trajectory path chooses a foot position, solves geometric IK, subtracts a neutral reference, and converts output-joint angle changes into raw motor-position changes. The motor driver still closes its joint loop; this description concerns the host trajectory command path.

Cycloidal swing-foot trajectory · 0 ≤ u ≤ 1
xswing = −L/2 + L[u − sin(2πu)/(2π)]
zlift = H[1 − cos(2πu)] / 2

L is step length, H is swing clearance, and u is normalized swing phase. This cycloidal foot-path shape is distinct from the cycloidal gearbox geometry.

From a geometric target to the motor
q(φ) = IK(p(φ))
Δq = q(φ) − IK(preference)
mtarget = mreference + σGΔq

σ is the configured motor sign and G is the gear ratio. In this inspected path, PDO2 sends position with desired velocity set to zero. Measured-position and telemetry readers exist elsewhere in the Python implementation.

leg_controller.py · output-joint delta to raw motor delta
def raw_delta_for_role(self, role: str, angle_delta: float) -> float:
    return get_motor_sign(self.name, role) * angle_delta * GEAR_RATIO

C++: command position and velocity explicitly

The C++ Cartesian path reconstructs foot position and velocity from measured joint state. It maps desired foot position through IK and desired foot velocity through the analytic Jacobian at the measured configuration, then validates and stages the joint commands.

State reconstruction and command construction
p̂ = FK(qmeasured)
v̂ = J(qmeasured)q̇measured
qdes = IK(pdes)
q̇des = (JᵀJ + λ²I)−1Jᵀvdes

The damped least-squares map reduces amplification near small singular values, with a tracking tradeoff. This is not a guarantee of stable physical motion.

LegController.cpp · solve instead of explicitly inverting
const Eigen::Matrix3d jacobian_transpose = forward_jacobian.transpose();
const Eigen::Matrix3d normal_matrix =
    jacobian_transpose * forward_jacobian +
    jacobian_damping * jacobian_damping * Eigen::Matrix3d::Identity();
return normal_matrix.ldlt().solve(jacobian_transpose);

The inspected PDO3 Cartesian command path sets feedforward torque to zero. Joint-layer checks cover position, position error, velocity, and feedforward-torque bounds before transmission. The presence of a torque field does not make this path a completed force or inverse-dynamics controller.

The equations changed with the conventions

This was more than a language change. The old Python model uses millimetres and a +84.26 mm hip offset. The retained C++ model uses metres, signed ±0.07456 m offsets, and explicit rigid transforms between leg and body frames.

Compare equal geometry before comparing raw angle tuples
X = ℓt sin t − ℓs sin(s − t)
A = ℓt cos t + ℓs cos(s − t)
pPython = [−X, ℓh cos h − A sin h, A cos h + ℓh sin h]ᵀ
pC++ = [X, ℓh cos h + A sin h, A cos h − ℓh sin h]ᵀ

These source equations expose different signs and joint conventions. They are an algebraic comparison, rather than a prescription for changing motor directions or calibration.

A revision trail I can return to

  1. May–June 2026

    Geometric Python prototype

    The tracked Python FK/IK and motor-interface files retain the earlier geometric convention.

  2. July 30, 2026

    Compare IK increments with a Jacobian update

    A C++ comparison tool computes IK(pnext) − IK(pnow) alongside a damped-Jacobian position increment and writes CSV results. Finite steps and damping mean these quantities need not be identical.

  3. September 9, 2026

    Move toward matrix and vector state

    The controller history records refactoring toward matrix/vector-based state and commands.

  4. October 17–18, 2026

    Revisit the Jacobian and frame convention

    The history records “New jacobian,” “frame convention improved,” and a return to the retained analytical FK/IK/Jacobian convention. Independent derivation then checks that convention.

Evaluate the mathematics and the robot separately

The saved MATLAB comparison covers 6,000 poses and 3,200 ideal command intervals for a recorded October 18 model snapshot. Maximum retained-versus-derived joint-increment difference is 8.89 × 10−16 rad. This establishes numerical agreement for that study; it is not a measurement of motor tracking.

WHAT THIS ESTABLISHES

The current work still needs physical calibration and tracking checks.

The single-leg comparison is diagnostic. Encoder-derived FK is a reconstruction, rather than an independent foot-position measurement. Some current controller files differ from the saved verification snapshot. Robust gait behavior and hardware performance need their own tests.
